# Fetch every link and keep a snapshot that outlives its site

## Intent

A link is only worth keeping if it can still be read when the site behind it changes or disappears. This package fetches every link a user adds, in the background and courteously, records what the page is (its title, description, icon, language and final address), stores the page itself as a snapshot and a cleaned reader view (a PDF whole, with its text), and lets the owner read either one from Alexandria at any time, as a use of the link, even when the origin is down or gone. The stream updates in place as fetches complete, and every fetch and its outcome is visible on the link.

## Goals

- Within 60 seconds of a link being added (p95), the page at its URL is fetched and the stream shows its title without a reload.
- Every successfully fetched link has a stored snapshot and a cleaned reader view that render even when the original site is down or gone; a link to a PDF has the whole PDF stored and readable.
- The fetcher never makes more than 1 request per second to the same host.
- Every failure is visible on the link as a state and a reason, and a link that cannot be fetched stays usable.
- Snapshots and reader views are never served to anyone but the owner, and are deleted with their link.

## Non-goals

- Enrichment (summary, tags, topic), the AI provider key and manual edits of title, summary, tags and topic: package 03 (`ai_enrichment`). This package stores the reader-view text that enrichment reads and says which links have no text to enrich.
- Liveness checks and the `dead` mark: package 05 (`decay_and_liveness`), which reuses this package's per-host rate limit.
- Search over the reader-view text: package 06 (`search_and_browse`). Workspaces (04), bulk import (07), the MCP server (08) and export (09) are their own packages.
- Crawling beyond the page at the pasted URL: linked pages, feeds and sitemaps are not fetched.
- Full-fidelity archiving of web pages (images, scripts, screenshots). The snapshot of a web page is its HTML and cleaned text; a PDF is the exception and is stored whole.
- Respecting `robots.txt`. Fetching is done on the owner's behalf, as a browser would; the only courtesy is the per-host rate limit.
- Offline / PWA operation of the website: the snapshot is for reading when the origin is gone, not when the reader is offline.
- Cross-user de-duplication of fetching: each user's URL is fetched and stored for that user alone, even when another user holds the same URL.

## Background

Package 01 (`accounts_links_and_stream`) creates the project: the Hono Worker in `src/worker/` with D1 (`DB`), the React website in `src/web/`, the allow-listed Google sign-in, sessions and personal access tokens, the error envelope and rate limit in `src/worker/api/`, the OpenAPI document that a test keeps in step with the routes, cursor pagination, and the shared test helpers `src/worker/test/helpers.ts` and `src/web/test/helpers.tsx`. Its links are added by `POST /api/v1/links` and `POST /api/v1/links/batch` in state `pending` with the host as provisional title and stay `pending` forever, because nothing fetches them. `recordUse` in `src/worker/links/use.ts` records a use (use count, last used, a `link_uses` row); `GET /api/v1/links/{id}/history` lists a link's `use` events; `LinkCard.tsx` and `LinkDetail.tsx` show a link on the website; `DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}` deletes a link and its uses. URLs are normalised and checked by `normalizeUrl` in `src/worker/links/normalize.ts`, which rejects localhost, loopback and private hosts.

This package adds the background fetch (a Cloudflare Queue and its consumer), the per-host rate limit (a Durable Object), the snapshot store (R2), the reader view, and the Read and Snapshot views.

Constraints the owner has set:

- Constraint: TypeScript throughout; Cloudflare services where they fit; external libraries only from very well-maintained projects.
- Constraint: strict per-user separation of data and processing.
- Constraint: `robots.txt` is not consulted (owner's decision).

## Requirements

### Fetch

- Within 60 seconds of a link being added (p95), the page at its URL is fetched: method GET, following at most 5 redirects, timeout 15 seconds, response body limit 5 MB, `Accept: text/html, application/pdf`, a User-Agent that identifies the service by name and gives a URL explaining it. Responses with a `text/html` or `application/xhtml+xml` content type are processed as web pages; responses with `application/pdf` (or a URL ending in `.pdf` whose response is a PDF) as PDFs, with a body limit of 50 MB instead of 5 MB. `robots.txt` is not consulted; the fetcher never makes more than 1 request per second to the same host.
- From a successful fetch the following are stored for the link: the final URL after redirects, the HTTP status, the page title (`<title>`, falling back to `og:title`, falling back to the host), the description (`og:description` / `meta description`), the favicon URL, the language if declared, the raw HTML (the **snapshot**) and the cleaned reader view. Link state becomes `active`.
- From a successful PDF fetch: the whole PDF file is stored as the snapshot, the title is the PDF's title metadata, falling back to the last path segment; the text of the document is extracted (first 500,000 characters) as the reader-view text. A PDF with no extractable text (scanned images) is `active` with a note "no text in this PDF".
- Failures, each visible on the link as a state and a reason:
  - fetch fails (DNS, connection, timeout, TLS): the link stays `pending` and is retried after 10 minutes and again after 2 hours; after the third failure it becomes `unreachable` with the reason shown ("could not connect", "timed out", ...), keeps its host as title, and can still be pinned, used and deleted.
  - HTTP 4xx/5xx: treated like a fetch failure, with the status shown ("HTTP 403").
  - a content type that is neither HTML nor PDF (an image, JSON, a video): the link becomes `active` with title = the final path segment or host, no snapshot, and a note "not a web page (image/png)".
  - page body over 5 MB: the first 5 MB are used, and the link is noted "truncated". PDF over 50 MB: not stored; the link is `active` with a note "PDF too large to store (50 MB limit)".
- Re-fetch: the user can request "refresh" on any link; it re-runs the fetch, replaces the snapshot and reader view, and records the new fetch time. At most one refresh per link per 10 minutes; a second within that window is refused with "already refreshed recently".
- The new link appears immediately with its host name as a provisional title and a `pending` indicator; the fetch runs in the background and the stream updates in place when it completes, without a reload.
- The link detail view shows the history of uses and fetches.

### Reader view and snapshot

- For every link with a snapshot the website offers "Read" (the cleaned reader view: article title, byline and body text with headings, lists, code blocks, links and inline images referenced by their original URL, nothing else) and "Snapshot" (the raw stored HTML rendered in a sandboxed frame with scripts disabled). Both work when the origin is unreachable. Both count as a use.
- For a PDF link, "Read" shows the extracted text and "Snapshot" serves the stored PDF itself, inline in the browser's PDF viewer, with a download action.
- Cleaning uses a Readability-style extraction. If extraction yields fewer than 200 characters of text, the reader view says "no readable content extracted" and offers the snapshot instead.
- Reader-view text is stored for search; the stored text is capped at 500,000 characters per link.
- Snapshots and reader views are deleted with their link, and are never served to any user other than the owner.

### End-to-end flows

1. The owner pastes the URL of a reachable article; it appears as `pending`; within a minute the card shows the article's title without a reload; the owner chooses "Read" and sees the cleaned article, and the card's last used is now.
2. A site goes offline after its page was fetched; the owner opens "Snapshot" and "Read" and both still show the stored page.
3. The owner pastes the URL of a PDF; the card shows the PDF's title; "Snapshot" shows the PDF inline with a download action and "Read" shows its text.

## Design Decisions

1. **"Archive" and "snapshot" are separate things.** Every successfully fetched link gets a snapshot immediately; "archived" is a lifecycle state handled in package 05. (Source PRD decision 1.)
2. **PDFs are in scope and stored whole**, up to 50 MB, with text extracted for reading and later search and enrichment. Owner's decision; the 50 MB figure is a per-deployment limit.
3. **robots.txt is not consulted**; the per-host rate limit of 1 request per second is the only courtesy. Owner's decision.
4. **The per-host rate limit is per host across all users**, not per user: one Durable Object per host spaces every request Alexandria sends to it (fetch, refresh, and package 05's liveness checks) at least 1 second apart. Decided in this run: it satisfies the source PRD's per-user rule and is the stricter courtesy, and it shares no user data.
5. **Fetching runs on a Cloudflare Queue** (`FETCH_QUEUE`): adding a link (one or a batch) and refresh each send one message; retries are the same message sent again with a delay of 10 minutes and then 2 hours. Decided in this run: a queue gives the background work its own retries and concurrency without blocking the request that added the link.
6. **Redirect targets are checked like pasted URLs.** A redirect to a non-http(s) scheme, localhost, a loopback, private or link-local address is a fetch failure with the reason "blocked address", so that a pasted public URL cannot make Alexandria read a private network. Decided in this run.
7. **The User-Agent** is `Alexandria/1.0 (+<PUBLIC_ORIGIN>/about/fetcher)`, and `/about/fetcher` is a public page explaining the fetcher. Decided in this run: the source PRD asks for a name and an explaining URL.
8. **A failed refresh keeps what the link had.** A refresh that fails (any fetch failure) leaves the previous snapshot, reader view, metadata and state in place, records a failed fetch event with its reason, and is not retried; only a link still `pending` follows the 10-minute / 2-hour retry chain. Decided in this run: a transient error must not take a working link's snapshot away; whether a link is dead is package 05's liveness check.
9. **The refresh limit answers 429.** A second refresh within 10 minutes answers 429 `{ "error": "refreshed_recently", "message": "already refreshed recently" }` with `Retry-After` in seconds; it is a rate limit, and package 01's convention gives rate limits 429.
10. **Where things are stored.** The snapshot (HTML or PDF) and the reader view's HTML are R2 objects under `u/{user_id}/l/{link_id}/`; the reader-view plain text (at most 500,000 characters) is a D1 row in `link_texts`, so that package 06 can index it; fetch events are rows of `link_events`. Decided in this run.
11. **The stream updates by polling.** While any loaded card is `pending`, the website asks `GET /api/v1/links?changed_since=<server time>` every 5 seconds and replaces changed cards in place. Decided in this run: polling needs no long-lived connection on Workers and meets the 60-second goal with room.
12. **The snapshot is served with a sandbox Content-Security-Policy** (`sandbox; default-src 'none'; img-src * data:; style-src * 'unsafe-inline'; font-src * data:`) and shown in an `<iframe sandbox>`, so stored scripts never run and the page cannot act on the owner's session. Decided in this run.
13. **Test seam for outbound requests.** When the deployment variable `ORIGIN_PROXY_URL` is set (end-to-end tests only), the fetcher sends each request to that URL with the target in the `X-Alexandria-Target` header, so that `e2e/fake-origin.ts` can play every origin site; all checks on the target (scheme, blocked address, redirects, limits) apply to the target URL. Production leaves it unset. Decided in this run: package 01's normaliser rejects localhost, so a local fake site cannot be pasted directly.
14. **A PDF that cannot be parsed** is treated like one without text: stored, `active`, noted "no text in this PDF". Decided in this run.
15. **The public page `/about/fetcher`** is the only page besides `/signin` served without a session, because the User-Agent points site operators at it. Decided in this run.
16. **Every write to a link sets its `updated_at`**, which the change feed `changed_since` reads; this package adds the column to package 01's links. Decided in this run.
17. **Deleting a link deletes its stored objects**, and a fetch message for a link deleted meanwhile is dropped without writing anything. Decided in this run, from the source PRD's "deleted with their link".

## Dependencies

- Package 01 `accounts_links_and_stream` (draft at the time of writing): the links, `recordUse`, the history endpoint, the API conventions, the OpenAPI document, the stream page and card, the test helpers and the project tooling. This package changes its add, batch and delete routes (to send fetch messages and delete stored objects), its history endpoint (to add `fetch` events) and its card and detail page.
- External: Cloudflare Queues, R2 and Durable Objects; every origin site a link points at.

## Verified External API

Read from the published packages on 2026-11-07:

- `@mozilla/readability` 0.6.0: `new Readability(document: Document, options?)`; `parse(): null | { title, content, textContent, length, excerpt, byline, dir, siteName, lang, publishedTime }`.
- `linkedom` 0.18.15: `parseHTML(html: string): Window & typeof globalThis`.
- `unpdf` 2.1.0: `getDocumentProxy(data, options?): Promise<PDFDocumentProxy>`; `extractText(data, { mergePages: true }): Promise<{ totalPages: number; text: string }>`; `getMeta(data, options?): Promise<{ info: PDFInfo; metadata }>`.
- `dompurify` 3.4.17: published and current; the website sanitises the reader view again with it before display (no symbol beyond its default `sanitize` relied on, not read).
- `hono` 4.13.17 and `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.23.0 as in package 01.

## Glossary

- **snapshot**: the raw HTML stored at fetch time, or for a PDF the whole file.
- **reader view**: the cleaned, content-only rendering extracted from the snapshot (for a PDF, its extracted text).
- **fetch event**: one fetch attempt recorded on a link, with its time, outcome, HTTP status and reason.
- **host gate**: the per-host rate limit, at most 1 request per second to one host.
- **use**: an open, read or snapshot view of a link, recorded with a timestamp.
- **unreachable**: the state of a link whose first fetch failed three times.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Fetching a link's page

**Rationale:** Everything the library knows about a link beyond its URL comes from one courteous GET of its page.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a link is added by POST /api/v1/links or POST /api/v1/links/batch with the outcome 'added', THE Alexandria API SHALL send one fetch message {user_id, link_id} on FETCH_QUEUE for that link, and none for a boosted or refused URL
   → exactly one FETCH_QUEUE message per added link, sent before the add request is answered
   Check: unit
   - setup: FETCH_QUEUE observed through the test helpers' queue recorder
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: seed 'https://c.example'; api('POST', '/api/v1/links/batch', {body: {urls: ['https://a.example', 'https://b.example', 'https://c.example', 'nope']}}); assert the recorded messages == [{user_id, link_id: a}, {user_id, link_id: b}]; api('POST', '/api/v1/links', {body: {url: 'https://d.example'}}); assert one more message for d
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the fetch worker receives a fetch message for an existing link, THE fetch worker SHALL send GET to the link's URL with 'Accept: text/html, application/pdf' and 'User-Agent: Alexandria/1.0 (+<PUBLIC_ORIGIN>/about/fetcher)', following at most 5 redirects and recording the URL of the last response as the final URL
   → fetchPage(url) returns {ok: true, finalUrl, status, contentType, body}; the origin receives the two headers on every request
   Check: unit
   - setup: the Worker's outbound requests answered by the fake origin of src/worker/test/origin.ts
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {a page answering 200 directly; a chain of exactly 5 redirects ending in 200}: r = fetchPage(start); assert r.ok and r.finalUrl == the chain's last URL; assert every request the fake origin logged carried Accept 'text/html, application/pdf' and the User-Agent with PUBLIC_ORIGIN + '/about/fetcher'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF a response redirects a sixth time, or redirects to a URL whose scheme is not http or https or whose host is localhost, a loopback, private or link-local address, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL stop following without requesting the redirect target and report the fetch as failed
   → fetchPage returns {ok: false, reason: 'too many redirects'} or {ok: false, reason: 'blocked address'}; the fake origin logs no request to the refused target
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {a chain of 6 redirects: 'too many redirects'; Location 'http://127.0.0.1/admin': 'blocked address'; Location 'http://169.254.169.254/latest': 'blocked address'; Location 'file:///etc/passwd': 'blocked address'}: r = fetchPage(start); assert r == {ok: false, reason}; assert the refused target was never requested
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the origin has not delivered the complete response within the fetch timeout of 15 seconds, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL abort the request and report the fetch as failed
   → fetchPage returns {ok: false, reason: 'timed out'} no later than 1 second after the timeout
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: a fake origin route that sends headers and then stalls; r = fetchPage(url, {timeoutMs: 200}); assert r == {ok: false, reason: 'timed out'} and the elapsed time < 1200 ms; and fetchPage's default timeoutMs used by the queue consumer is 15000
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE host gate SHALL for any host, space every request Alexandria sends to that host at least 1 second apart, across all users, links, refreshes and background jobs, without delaying requests to other hosts
   Check: integration
   - setup: the HOST_GATE Durable Object running in the Workers test runtime
   - setup: the fake origin recording the arrival time of each request
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: two users each add 3 links on host same.example and 1 link on other.example; deliver all 8 fetch messages concurrently; assert the arrival times at same.example, sorted, differ by >= 1000 ms pairwise-adjacent; assert the other.example request arrived within 500 ms of delivery
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] THE fetch worker SHALL for any fetch, request only the link's URL and the redirects it follows, never robots.txt, the favicon, or any page, image or feed the fetched page refers to
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: the fake origin serves an HTML page referring to /robots.txt, an icon, images, a stylesheet and links; process the link's fetch message; assert the fake origin's log is exactly [GET of the link's URL]
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] WHEN anyone requests GET /about/fetcher, signed in or not, THE Alexandria API SHALL serve a public page naming Alexandria's fetcher, saying that it fetches only pages its users add, at most once per second per host, and does not read robots.txt
   → HTTP 200 text/html without a session, whose text contains 'Alexandria' and '1 request per second'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: r = SELF.fetch('/about/fetcher', {redirect: 'manual'}) without cookies; assert r.status == 200 and content-type starts with 'text/html' and the body contains 'Alexandria' and '1 request per second'
   ```

### REQ-2: Storing a fetched web page

**Rationale:** The first fetch turns a bare URL into a recognisable card and a copy that survives the site.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a fetch receives a 2xx response with content type text/html or application/xhtml+xml, THE fetch worker SHALL store the final URL, HTTP status, title, description, favicon URL, language and fetch time on the link, store the raw HTML as the snapshot and the reader view, and set the link's state to 'active'
   → GET /api/v1/links/{id} returns state 'active', final_url, http_status, title, description, favicon_url, language, fetched_at and content_kind 'html'; the R2 object u/{user_id}/l/{link_id}/snapshot holds the response body
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: the fake origin serves a fixture article at https://news.example/a after one redirect; add the link and process its message; l = api('GET', '/api/v1/links/' + id).json; assert l.state == 'active' and l.final_url == the redirect target and l.http_status == 200 and l.title == the fixture's <title> and l.content_kind == 'html'; assert SNAPSHOTS.get(prefix + 'snapshot') bytes == the fixture
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE fetch worker SHALL for any fetched HTML, take the title from <title>, else og:title, else the host; the description from og:description, else meta description, else none; the favicon URL from the first link whose rel contains 'icon', resolved against the final URL, else the final URL's origin plus /favicon.ico; and the language from the html element's lang attribute, else none; with surrounding whitespace trimmed and inner runs of whitespace collapsed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/html.test.ts, a table of (html, finalUrl, expected metadata) covering: <title> present; empty <title> with og:title; neither (title == host); og:description over meta description; meta description only; no description (null); <link rel='shortcut icon' href='/i.png'> resolved to an absolute URL; no icon link (origin + '/favicon.ico'); <html lang='de'>; no lang (null); a title with newlines and double spaces: assert extractMetadata(html, finalUrl) == expected
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF an HTML response body is larger than 5 MB, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL read only its first 5 MB, store and process them as the page, and note the link as truncated
   → the link is 'active' with notes containing 'truncated'; the snapshot object is exactly 5,242,880 bytes
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: the fake origin streams a 6 MB HTML page; process the fetch; assert state 'active', notes include 'truncated' and the snapshot object's size == 5242880
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF a 2xx response has a content type that is neither HTML nor PDF, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL set the link 'active' with the final URL's last path segment, else its host, as title, store no snapshot and no reader view, and note it as not a web page with its content type
   → the link is 'active' with content_kind 'other', title as stated and notes containing 'not a web page (<content type>)'; no R2 object exists under the link's prefix
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {https://img.example/photos/cat.png as image/png: title 'cat.png', note 'not a web page (image/png)'; https://api.example/ as application/json: title 'api.example', note 'not a web page (application/json)'}: process; assert state, content_kind, title, note; assert SNAPSHOTS.list(prefix) is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF the link of a fetch message is deleted before or while the fetch worker processes it, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL write nothing for it, remove any object already written under its prefix, and acknowledge the message
   → no links row and no R2 object for the link exist afterwards; the message is acknowledged and not retried
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {deleted before delivery; deleted while the fake origin holds the response}: process the message; assert no row for the id, SNAPSHOTS.list(prefix) empty and message.ack called once
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] IF writing the snapshot to R2 or the link's row to D1 fails while a fetch result is stored, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL leave the link as it was before the attempt, remove any object written by the attempt, and hand the message back to the queue for redelivery without counting a fetch attempt
   → the links row equals its state before the attempt (fetch_attempts unchanged); message.retry is called; no partial object remains
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {SNAPSHOTS.put throws; the D1 update throws}, injected through the store's test hooks: process; assert the link row is unchanged, message.retry called, SNAPSHOTS.list(prefix) empty
   ```

### REQ-3: Storing PDFs

**Rationale:** Papers and manuals arrive as PDFs, and the owner wants the whole file kept.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a fetch receives a 2xx response with content type application/pdf, or a response for a URL whose path ends in '.pdf' whose body starts with '%PDF-', THE fetch worker SHALL store the whole PDF as the snapshot, take the title from the PDF's Title metadata, else the last path segment, store the extracted text up to its first 500,000 characters as the reader-view text, and set the link 'active'
   → the link is 'active' with content_kind 'pdf' and the title as stated; the snapshot object holds the exact PDF bytes; GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader returns the extracted text
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/pdf.test.ts, a table over {fixture paper.pdf with Title 'On Links' served as application/pdf: title 'On Links'; the same file without Title served as application/octet-stream at /docs/manual.pdf: title 'manual.pdf'}: process; assert state 'active', content_kind 'pdf', title, snapshot bytes == the fixture, and reader text starts with the fixture's first sentence
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF a stored PDF yields no extractable text, or cannot be parsed, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL keep the stored PDF, set the link 'active' with no reader-view text and note that the PDF has no text
   → the link is 'active' with notes containing 'no text in this PDF'; the snapshot object exists; GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader returns {empty: true}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/pdf.test.ts, a table over {a scanned-image fixture with no text layer; a truncated, unparseable PDF}: process; assert state 'active', note 'no text in this PDF', snapshot present, reader.empty == true
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF a PDF response is larger than 50 MB, by its Content-Length or by the bytes read, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL stop reading it, store nothing, and set the link 'active' with the last path segment as title and a note that the PDF is too large
   → the link is 'active' with content_kind 'pdf' and notes containing 'PDF too large to store (50 MB limit)'; no R2 object exists under the link's prefix; no more than 50 MB plus one read chunk was read
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/pdf.test.ts, a table over {Content-Length 60 MB; no Content-Length and a 60 MB streamed body}: process; assert state, note, SNAPSHOTS.list(prefix) empty, and the fake origin's bytes-sent counter <= 50 MB + 64 KB
   ```

### REQ-4: Fetch failures and retries

**Rationale:** Sites are down for a while all the time; the link must wait, retry and then say plainly why it failed, without becoming useless.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] IF the first or second fetch attempt of a 'pending' link fails by DNS, connection, TLS, timeout, too many redirects, blocked address or an HTTP 4xx or 5xx status, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL keep the link 'pending' with the failure's reason, count the attempt, record a failed fetch event, and send the fetch message again with a delay of 10 minutes after the first failure and 2 hours after the second
   → state 'pending', fetch_attempts 1 or 2, state_reason set; one FETCH_QUEUE message re-sent with delaySeconds 600 or 7200
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: the fake origin answers 503 for the link; process attempt 1; assert state 'pending', fetch_attempts 1, state_reason 'HTTP 503', a re-sent message with delaySeconds 600; process attempt 2; assert fetch_attempts 2 and delaySeconds 7200
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF the third fetch attempt of a 'pending' link fails, THEN THE fetch worker SHALL set the link 'unreachable' with the last failure's reason, keep its host as title, record a failed fetch event and send no further fetch message
   → state 'unreachable', state_reason the last reason, title the host; no FETCH_QUEUE message sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts beside the test above: process attempt 3 with the fake origin refusing connections; assert state 'unreachable', state_reason 'could not connect', title == host and no message sent
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE fetch worker SHALL for any fetch failure, state its reason as 'host not found' for a DNS failure, 'could not connect' for a refused or reset connection, 'TLS error' for a certificate or handshake failure, 'timed out', 'too many redirects', 'blocked address', or 'HTTP <status>' for a 4xx or 5xx response
   → fetchPage returns {ok: false, reason: <the reason>}, and the same reason becomes the link's state_reason and the fetch event's reason
   Check: unit

1. [REQ-4.4] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any 'unreachable' link, keep it in the stream and let the owner open, pin, unpin, refresh and delete it like any other link
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: make a link 'unreachable' through three failed attempts; assert it is in GET /api/v1/links; a table over {open: 302, pin: 200, unpin: 200, refresh: 202, delete: 204}: assert each status
   ```

### REQ-5: Extracting the reader view

**Rationale:** Reading the stored article means its words without the site's chrome, and nothing from the stored page may run.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE reader SHALL for any stored HTML page, produce the reader view with Readability over a DOM of the snapshot, keeping the article title, byline and body with headings, paragraphs, lists, code blocks, links and inline images, with every link and image address made absolute against the final URL, and nothing else
   Check: unit

   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/reader.test.ts, a table over fixtures {a blog article with nav, sidebar, comments and footer; a documentation page with <pre><code> blocks and nested lists; an article with relative <img src='img/a.png'> and <a href='/b'>}: r = extractReader(html, finalUrl); assert r.title and r.byline match the fixture; assert r.html contains the article's headings, list items and code blocks; assert nav, sidebar, comments and footer text are absent; assert the image src and link href are absolute URLs on the final URL's origin
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] THE reader SHALL for any HTML input, return reader HTML that contains no script, style, iframe, frame, form, input, button, object or embed element, no attribute whose name starts with 'on', and no URL with a scheme other than http, https or data:image
   Check: property
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/reader.test.ts: for generated article pages into which random positions get <script>, <style>, <iframe>, <form><input>, <object>, <embed>, onclick/onerror/onload attributes and javascript: and vbscript: hrefs (in mixed case and with entity-encoded characters): out = extractReader(page, url).html; parse out; assert none of the elements, no on* attribute and no href or src outside the allowed schemes
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] IF the reader extraction of a stored HTML page yields fewer than 200 characters of text, THEN THE reader SHALL store the reader view as empty, keeping the snapshot, so that Read offers the snapshot instead
   → GET /api/v1/links/{id}/reader returns {empty: true, html: null, text: ''}; the snapshot is still served
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/reader.test.ts, a table over {a page whose article text is 199 characters: empty; one with exactly 200: not empty; a page of only images: empty}: process the fetch; assert reader.empty as stated and GET snapshot answers 200
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] THE reader SHALL for any link, store at most the first 500,000 characters of its reader-view text, for web pages and PDFs alike
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/reader.test.ts, a table over {an HTML article of 600,000 characters of text; a PDF fixture whose text is 700,000 characters; an article of 1,000 characters}: process; assert the length of link_texts.text == min(length, 500000) and it equals the first characters of the extracted text
   ```

   → HTTP 200 with body {content_kind: 'html' | 'pdf', title, byline, html: string | null, text: string, empty: boolean}; use_count is one higher and last_used_at is the request time

1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN a user requests GET /api/v1/links/{id}/snapshot for one of their links whose snapshot is HTML, THE Alexandria API SHALL record a use and return the stored HTML with headers that disable its scripts and isolate it from the site

### REQ-7: Refreshing a link

**Rationale:** Pages change; the owner can take a new copy, but not hammer a site with it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a user requests POST /api/v1/links/{id}/refresh for one of their links that has not been refreshed in the last 10 minutes, THE Alexandria API SHALL send a refresh fetch message for it; when the fetch succeeds, replace the snapshot, reader view and fetched metadata, set the link 'active', clear its reason and notes, and record the new fetch time
   → HTTP 202 with body {status: 'queued'}; after the message is processed the link's fetched_at is the new fetch time and the snapshot holds the new body
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts, a table over {an 'active' link whose page has changed; an 'unreachable' link whose site is back}: r = api('POST', '/api/v1/links/' + id + '/refresh'); assert 202 {status: 'queued'}; process the message; assert state 'active', state_reason null, fetched_at == now and the snapshot equals the new body
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF a refresh of a link is requested less than 10 minutes after the previous refresh request of that link, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse it without sending a fetch message
   → HTTP 429 with body {"error": "refreshed_recently", "message": "already refreshed recently"} and Retry-After equal to the whole seconds left in the window; no FETCH_QUEUE message
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: refresh at t; setNow(t + 4 min); r = refresh; assert 429, the body, Retry-After == 360 and no new message; setNow(t + 10 min); assert refresh answers 202
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] IF the fetch of a refresh fails, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL keep the link's previous state, snapshot, reader view and metadata, record a failed fetch event with the reason, and send no retry
   → the link's row and R2 objects equal their values before the refresh; one more fetch event {outcome: 'failed', reason}; no FETCH_QUEUE message
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts: fetch an article; switch the fake origin to 500; refresh and process; assert state 'active', title and snapshot unchanged; history's newest event is {kind: 'fetch', outcome: 'failed', reason: 'HTTP 500'}; no message sent
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] WHEN the owner chooses Refresh on a card or on a link's detail page, THE website SHALL send the refresh request, show the card as refreshing, and show 'already refreshed recently' when the API answers refreshed_recently
   → one POST /api/v1/links/{id}/refresh per click; a 429 refreshed_recently shows 'already refreshed recently'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/components/LinkCard.test.tsx with a fake API: click Refresh; assert one POST .../refresh and a refreshing indicator; with the fake answering 429 refreshed_recently assert 'already refreshed recently' is shown
   ```

[REQ-8.3] WHILE the stream page holds at least one card whose link is 'pending' or being refreshed, THE website SHALL ask for the links changed since the last server time every 5 seconds and replace each changed card in place, without a reload and without moving the other cards, stopping when no such card remains

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A pasted article is fetched, shown in place and read

1. **owner** pastes the URL of a reachable article into the add input and presses Enter
2. **Alexandria API** stores the link as 'pending' and sends a fetch message on FETCH_QUEUE
3. **website** shows the card at the top with the host as title and a pending indicator, and starts polling for changes
4. **fetch worker** waits for the host gate, fetches the page, stores the metadata, the snapshot in R2 and the reader view, and sets the link 'active'
5. **website** receives the changed link and shows the article's title and favicon on the same card without a reload
6. **owner** chooses Read on the card
7. **Alexandria API** records a use and returns the stored reader view
8. **website** shows the article's title, byline and body

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, FETCH_QUEUE, fetch worker, HOST_GATE, R2 bucket SNAPSHOTS, D1 database, Readability extraction

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local D1, R2, Queues and Durable Objects
- ORIGIN_PROXY_URL points at e2e/fake-origin.ts, which plays https://news.example/article with a fixture article (the origin site is the only stubbed party besides e2e/fake-google.ts)
- the owner signed in

**End state:**

- the card shows the fixture's title within 60 seconds of Enter, with no page reload
- the R2 object u/{user_id}/l/{link_id}/snapshot holds the fixture HTML and link_texts holds its text
- the Read page shows the fixture's headline and first paragraph
- the link's use_count is 1 and its history lists one fetch and one use

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/fetch.spec.ts: sign in; paste 'https://news.example/article' and press Enter; record the page's navigation count; expect the first card's title to become 'An Article' within 60 s and the navigation count unchanged; click Read; expect the headline and first paragraph; request GET /api/v1/links/{id} and /history and assert use_count 1 and the two events
```

### PATH-2: A stored page is read after its site goes offline

1. **owner** adds the URL of a reachable article
2. **fetch worker** fetches it and stores the snapshot and reader view
3. **origin site** goes offline and refuses every connection
4. **owner** chooses Snapshot on the card
5. **Alexandria API** serves the stored HTML under the sandbox policy without contacting the origin
6. **owner** chooses Read on the card
7. **Alexandria API** serves the stored reader view

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, fetch worker, R2 bucket SNAPSHOTS, D1 database

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local bindings; e2e/fake-origin.ts plays the article and can be switched to refuse connections; the owner signed in

**End state:**

- the Snapshot frame shows the stored page's headline while the fake origin refuses connections
- the Read page shows the stored article
- the fake origin logged no request after it went offline
- the link's use_count is 2

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/fetch.spec.ts: add the article and wait for 'active'; fakeOrigin.goOffline(); click Snapshot; expect the sandboxed frame to contain the headline; click Read; expect the article text; assert fakeOrigin.requestsSince(offline) == 0 and use_count == 2
```

### PATH-3: A pasted PDF is stored whole and read

1. **owner** pastes the URL of a PDF
2. **Alexandria API** stores the link as 'pending' and sends a fetch message
3. **fetch worker** fetches the PDF, stores the whole file, extracts its title and text, and sets the link 'active'
4. **owner** chooses Snapshot and sees the PDF in the browser's viewer with a Download action
5. **Alexandria API** serves the stored PDF inline, and as an attachment for Download
6. **owner** chooses Read and sees the PDF's text

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, FETCH_QUEUE, fetch worker, PDF text extraction, R2 bucket SNAPSHOTS, D1 database

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local bindings; e2e/fake-origin.ts serves https://papers.example/on-links.pdf, a fixture PDF titled 'On Links'; the owner signed in

**End state:**

- the card's title is 'On Links'
- the snapshot response is application/pdf with the fixture's exact bytes, inline; the Download response is an attachment
- the Read page shows the fixture's first sentence

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/fetch.spec.ts: paste the PDF URL; expect the card title 'On Links' within 60 s; click Snapshot; expect an embedded viewer whose src answers application/pdf with the fixture bytes; follow Download and expect Content-Disposition attachment; click Read and expect the first sentence
```
